desc:
Encoding. A non-negative integer is stored as an array of its decimal digits, most significant digit first, one digit per element, with no leading zeros; the number zero is stored as [0]. Results use the same format. The numbers can have thousands of digits, so you cannot convert a whole array into one machine integer.

Add the numbers a and b column by column the way you do on paper, starting at the units column. A carry operation happens in a column when the digit sum of that column (including the carry coming in from the right) is 10 or more, so a 1 is carried into the next column. Return how many carry operations the addition needs.

Example: a = [4,5], b = [5,5] (45 + 55). The units column gives 5 + 5 = 10, a carry; the tens column gives 4 + 5 + 1 = 10, another carry. The answer is 2.

Example: a = [9,9,9], b = [1] (999 + 1): all three columns carry, so the answer is 3.
constraints: No leading zeros, except for the number zero stored as [0]
hints: Do exactly what you do on paper: go through the columns from the right, with a running carry.
The two arrays can have different lengths. Once one of them runs out, treat its missing digits as 0 (the other digits can still produce a carry).

Per column: s = carry + digitA + digitB; the new carry is 1 when s ≥ 10, else 0. Add the new carry to your counter. Stop after the longer array is done (a final carry creates no further column to count).
editorial: Walk both arrays from their right ends with two indices and one variable carry. In every column the sum is at most 9 + 9 + 1 = 19, so the carry out is always 0 or 1. Count the columns whose sum reaches 10.

The loop runs for max(a.length, b.length) columns. After the last column a leftover carry only becomes a new leading digit; it is not an extra carry operation because no addition happens in that new column. Time is linear and only a few variables are needed.
solution:
def countCarries(a, b):
    i, j = len(a) - 1, len(b) - 1
    carry = 0
    count = 0
    while i >= 0 or j >= 0:
        s = carry
        if i >= 0:
            s += a[i]
            i -= 1
        if j >= 0:
            s += b[j]
            j -= 1
        carry = 1 if s >= 10 else 0
        count += carry
    return count
